findings.title: Unused ServiceAccount holds cluster-admin-equivalent access cluster-wide (security-demo-overprivileged)
findings.detail: security-demo-overprivileged → ClusterRole security-demo-everything (risk 100/100). Grants: Full wildcard: every verb on every resource (cluster-admin equivalent). Subjects: ServiceAccount security-demo/ci-deployer. No pod or workload uses these ServiceAccounts, so the privilege serves nothing but anyone who can get a token for them inherits it.
findings.remediation: Delete the binding (and the ServiceAccount) if it is no longer needed; otherwise scope it down.

findings.title: Pod privileged-debug fails the baseline Pod Security profile
findings.detail: Fails 4 checks of the baseline profile and 6 more checks of the restricted profile. Baseline blocks known privilege escalations; a pod failing it can usually take over its node.
findings.remediation: Remove privileged mode, host namespaces, hostPath volumes and added capabilities unless this is a trusted node agent; then work towards the restricted profile.

findings.title: LoadBalancer Service web-public is exposed externally
findings.detail: Exposes Deployment web-latest (ports 31334→80, pending address) to any source, backed by Deployment web-latest. Its pods are not protected by any ingress NetworkPolicy, so every port they listen on is reachable.
findings.remediation: Set `loadBalancerSourceRanges` to the client CIDRs, use an internal load balancer, or put it behind an Ingress/Gateway with TLS and auth. Add an ingress NetworkPolicy for the backing pods.

findings.title: Pod privileged-debug uses the node's network namespace
findings.detail: Host networking bypasses NetworkPolicy and exposes ports directly on the node; with hostNetwork the pod can also see all node traffic and reach node-local services.
findings.remediation: Use a Service instead of hostPort, and drop hostNetwork unless this is a CNI/node agent.

findings.title: NetworkPolicy allow-all-ingress allows ingress from anywhere
findings.detail: A rule with no `from` peers or an ipBlock of 0.0.0.0/0 lets any source, including outside the cluster, reach pods matching app=web-latest.
findings.remediation: Restrict `from` to the namespaces/pods (or CIDRs) that need access, and the `ports` they need.

findings.title: nginx:latest has 1 critical CVE (no fix yet)
findings.detail: 1 critical (0 fixable), 12 high (0 fixable), 13 medium, 114 low. Top: CVE-2026-6653 (libxml2 2.12.7+dfsg+really2.9.14-2.1+deb13u3), CVE-2026-118370 (libexpat1 2.9.0-1~deb13u1), CVE-2025-69720 (libtinfo6 6.5+20250216-2), CVE-2026-117610 (libexpat1 2.9.0-1~deb13u1), CVE-2026-9538 (perl-base 5.40.1-6+deb13u1). Used by web-latest.
findings.remediation: Rebuild on a patched base image or bump to a release that includes the fixed package versions, then redeploy.

findings.title: Ingress web-plain-http serves web.example.test without TLS
findings.detail: Hosts without a `tls` entry are served over plain HTTP, so credentials and cookies travel unencrypted.
findings.remediation: Add a `spec.tls` entry with a certificate (e.g. from cert-manager) and redirect HTTP to HTTPS.

findings.title: 1 workload in security-demo uses :latest or untagged images
findings.detail: Floating tags make deployments unreproducible and can silently pull a different (possibly compromised) image on the next restart. Affected: Deployment web-latest (nginx:latest).
findings.remediation: Pin images to a version tag, ideally with a digest (`image@sha256:…`).

findings.title: 2 workloads in security-demo accept ingress from anywhere
findings.detail: security-demo has NetworkPolicies, but privileged-debug, web-latest are not selected by any policy that restricts ingress (or a policy re-opens it to 0.0.0.0/0).
findings.remediation: Add a default-deny ingress policy (`podSelector: {}`, `policyTypes: [Ingress]`) and allow only the traffic each workload needs.

findings.title: 1 namespace has no default-deny policy
findings.detail: security-demo have NetworkPolicies but no default-deny for ingress and egress, so new workloads start out unrestricted.
findings.remediation: Add a policy with `podSelector: {}` and no rules for each direction.

findings.title: RoleBinding ghost-reader refers to a missing Role secret-reader
findings.detail: The binding grants nothing today, but creating a Role named secret-reader would immediately grant it to ServiceAccount security-demo/deleted-bot.
findings.remediation: Delete the binding if it is stale.

findings.title: RoleBinding ghost-reader binds ServiceAccounts that don't exist
findings.detail: Missing: security-demo/deleted-bot. Anyone who creates a ServiceAccount with that name silently inherits Role secret-reader.
findings.remediation: Delete the stale binding, or remove the missing subjects from it.

findings.title: 1 namespace doesn't enforce a Pod Security level
findings.detail: security-demo have no `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce` label, so Pod Security admission lets any pod spec in (privileged included, unless another admission controller blocks it).
findings.remediation: Label namespaces with `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=baseline` (or `restricted`). Try `warn`/`audit` first to see what would break.

findings.title: Deployment web-latest (2 pods) does not meet the restricted Pod Security profile
findings.detail: Meets baseline but fails 5 checks of the restricted profile (current pod hardening best practice).
findings.remediation: Set `runAsNonRoot: true`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, `seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}`, `capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}` and `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` in the securityContext.

findings.title: 2 workloads in security-demo mount the default ServiceAccount token
findings.detail: These pods run as the namespace's `default` ServiceAccount with its API token mounted. Any permissions granted to `default` are shared by every such pod, and a compromised container gets an API credential for free. Affected: Pod privileged-debug, Deployment web-latest.
findings.remediation: Set `automountServiceAccountToken: false` on the pod (or the default ServiceAccount), or use a dedicated ServiceAccount.

findings.title: 1 workload in security-demo has containers without liveness or readiness probes
findings.detail: Without probes, Kubernetes sends traffic to containers that aren't ready and never restarts hung ones. Affected: Deployment web-latest (nginx).
findings.remediation: Add a readinessProbe (and a livenessProbe for processes that can hang).

findings.title: 2 workloads in security-demo have containers without resource limits or requests
findings.detail: Without a memory limit one container can exhaust the node (a noisy-neighbour or denial-of-service risk); without requests the scheduler can't place it sensibly. Affected: Pod privileged-debug (shell: memory limit, requests), Deployment web-latest (nginx: memory limit, requests).
findings.remediation: Set `resources.requests` for CPU and memory and a memory limit; a LimitRange can provide namespace defaults.

findings.title: 1 workload in security-demo exposes Secrets as environment variables
findings.detail: Environment variables leak into crash dumps, `/proc/<pid>/environ`, child processes and logs more easily than mounted files. Affected: Deployment web-latest (DB_PASSWORD).
findings.remediation: Mount Secrets as files (a `secret` volume) instead of env vars.

findings.title: 2 workloads in security-demo have unrestricted egress
findings.detail: privileged-debug, web-latest are not selected by any policy that restricts egress, so they can connect anywhere, including the internet and the cloud metadata endpoint.
findings.remediation: Add a default-deny egress policy and allow DNS plus the destinations each workload needs.

findings.title: Ingress web-plain-http exposes web.example.test
findings.detail: Routes web.example.test to services web-public, backed by Deployment web-latest. Its pods are not protected by any ingress NetworkPolicy, so every port they listen on is reachable.
findings.remediation: Confirm these hosts are meant to be public; add authentication at the ingress controller where needed.

findings.title: 1 Role in security-demo is not bound by anything
findings.detail: orphan-exec. Unbound roles grant nothing but clutter RBAC reviews.
findings.remediation: Delete roles that are no longer needed.
